data.long_meaning: Nikiforos is derived from the Greek words 'nikos' meaning victory and 'theos' meaning God. The name Nikiforos was given to those who were consecrated to God or who dedicated their lives to Him. The name Nikiforos carries the meaning “Victory of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Nikiforos usually hope their child will grow to embody victory of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: ניקיפורוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ניקיפורוס מקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו 'נושא הניצחון', התואמת את המושג הנוצרי של ישו המשיח כמושיע ומנצח על החטא והמוות. השם משקף את הנושא של ניצחון רוחני וחיי נצח.

in_greek.name: Νικηφόρος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Νικηφόρος προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'νίκη' (νίκη) και 'φόρος' (φορέας), που σημαίνει 'εκείνος που φέρνει τη νίκη'. Στο χριστιανικό πλαίσιο, το όνομα αυτό συμβολίζει τη νίκη επί του θανάτου και της αμαρτίας μέσω του Ιησού Χριστού.

in_latin.name: Nikiforos
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Nikiforos origine Graecum habet, compositum ex 'nike' (victoria) et 'phoros' (ferens), quod interpretatur 'victoriam ferens' seu 'qui victoriam apportat'. In traditione christiana, hoc nomen significat victoriam spiritualem et triumphum in peccato et morte per Iesum Christum.

in_english.name: Nikiforos
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nikiforos originates from Greek roots, specifically from 'nike' (victory) and 'phoros' (bearer). It translates to 'bringer of victory' or 'victorious'. In Christian tradition, Nikiforos symbolizes spiritual victory and triumph over sin and death through Jesus Christ. Historically, the name has been used in Eastern Orthodox cultures, reflecting the importance of achieving spiritual victory.

data.cultural_impact: Nikiforos was a popular name among the Byzantine Christians during the Middle Ages. It was given to individuals who were dedicated to spiritual pursuits or who were victorious in their faith. It was also a name given to those who held religious roles, such as clergy or monks.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Nikiforos holds significant spiritual meaning for Christians. It signifies the belief that God is the giver of victory and that one's life should be dedicated to Him. The name is a reminder of the importance of putting faith in God and relying on His divine power to overcome challenges and obstacles. It also represents the idea of being a consecrated vessel for God, and living a life that brings honor and glory to Him. Overall, the name Nikiforos embodies the Christian virtues of faith, dedication, and triumph over adversity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nikiforos, meaning "victory of Christ," symbolizes the triumph of faith over worldly struggles and the ultimate victory of the soul in Christ. It is a name deeply rooted in the spiritual journey of the Christian faith.

historical_references.reference: Nikiforos Phokas, a Byzantine general and emperor, was born around 960 in the village of Kastania, near Larissa, in Thessaly, Greece. He led a successful military campaign against the Seljuk Turks in 1001, which resulted in the capture of the city of Antioch. In 1002, he was made a patrician and appointed as the governor of Antioch. In 1003, he was recalled to Constantinople, where he was given the rank of magistros and appointed as the commander of the imperial guard.

Nikiforos Fokas, a medieval Greek monk, lived in the 14th century. He is best known for his 'Book of Miracles,' which describes numerous miracles attributed to various saints in the Orthodox tradition. The book was widely read and copied throughout the Eastern Orthodox world, and it is still used as a source of hagiographic information today.

modern_usage.modern_context: Nikiforos (Νικηφόρος) is a Greek name that translates to 'victory of the people'. However, in modern context, it is most commonly associated with the self-taught Russian artist Nikifor, born as Nikifor Timofeev (1895-1952). Known for his iconic folk art style, he was diagnosed with schizophrenia early in life and spent most of his life in institutions. His work has gained recognition in the art world and is often discussed in the context of outsider art and mental health. Nikifor's art is celebrated on platforms such as Wikipedia, where his biography and artworks are extensively documented, Artsy, an online platform for discovering, buying, and selling arts, and Saatchi Art, a leading online art gallery. The trends surrounding Nikiforos' name include icon painting, outsider art, mental health, and self-taught artists.
